nodes.label: Accuracy floors
nodes.note: P1 at 100 per cent by census, P2 at 99.5, P3 at 99.0. Below a floor the product changes behaviour rather than reporting a worse number.

nodes.label: Clean-room rule
nodes.note: Original items written from DfE-published content. No board text, no third-party revision material, and a positive declaration on every validation record.

nodes.label: Provenance labelling
nodes.note: The IT Amendment Rules 2026 require prominent labelling and permanent provenance metadata that cannot be stripped from synthetically generated information.

nodes.label: Promise P2
nodes.note: It only tells you things it can show you the source for, and says so when it cannot. Enforced as a runtime gate, not as a tolerance.

nodes.label: Pinned versions
nodes.note: A vendor update passes the frozen battery before it reaches a learner. We run behind the frontier and pay to qualify every upgrade.

nodes.label: Licence and kill-switch SLA
nodes.note: Fifteen minutes to disable, sixty seconds of cache, seven days to purge primary stores, thirty-five days for backups. A contractual commitment, not a setting.

nodes.label: Children's code and UK GDPR
nodes.note: Data minimisation, defaults off, and a lawful basis for profiling. The ICO has said it will audit edtech providers.

nodes.label: Online Safety Act scoping
nodes.note: The scoping decision and the trigger that reverses it. Ofcom penalties reach 10 per cent of qualifying worldwide revenue plus disruption orders.

nodes.label: Zero-retention terms
nodes.note: No vendor is used unless the contract provides zero retention of prompts and outputs and no training on our data. The marketing line is only true if the contract makes it true.

nodes.label: Outcome-claim discipline
nodes.note: What may be said to a parent about results, and the advertising and consumer regime that governs saying it.

nodes.label: Session canvas
nodes.note: One learner, one objective, fifteen to thirty minutes, on a phone held vertically. Diagrams must work at 360 CSS pixels and state must survive a fifteen-minute interruption.

nodes.label: Refusal notice
nodes.note: What the learner sees when the gate fires. A free chatbot would have answered the same question fluently, which is the price of P2.

nodes.label: Unaided check
nodes.note: Two or three held-out items, no hints, scored on first commit. Deliberately unpleasant, and the whole anti-surface-fluency mechanism.

nodes.label: Educator chooser
nodes.note: Picking a named educator whose teaching the student already recognises. The wedge, on the one screen that has to earn it.

nodes.label: Style controls
nodes.note: Six controls in plain language rather than twelve sliders, each mapping to one or two dimensions, with a one-tap return to the preset as licensed.

nodes.label: Practice paper
nodes.note: Assembled from validated items, and the mark scheme is called a CINE mark scheme everywhere a learner or a parent can see it.

nodes.label: Grade range display
nodes.note: A current performance band, never a prediction, suppressed below an evidence threshold, and hideable by the learner while the parent's report still shows it.

nodes.label: Parent report
nodes.note: The payer is the parent and the user is the child, and those two want measurably different things. That tension runs through this surface.

nodes.label: Adult verification
nodes.note: We never ask a child how old they are. We verify an adult and let them enrol a learner, and every learner account is treated as a child's account whatever anyone typed.

nodes.label: School console
nodes.note: Route B. Staff authenticate through the school's own identity provider and the school enrols its pupils under duties it already has.

nodes.label: Marketing site
nodes.note: Where the claims are made, where the board is named under a fixed convention, and where the one line about a child's data goes unedited.

nodes.label: Composer
nodes.note: Deterministic, no model call. Selects the objective, retrieves the permitted nodes, renders the style card and assembles the turn plan. The load-bearing step.

nodes.label: Generator
nodes.note: One model call on a pinned version, given the permitted sources and unable to reach outside them.

abs.why: Bought behind an abstraction and pinned, so a vendor change is contained here in shape. Its behaviour still travels.

nodes.label: Verifier
nodes.note: Four checks, all blocking, on a different pinned model from the generator. A verifier that shared the generator's weights would share its errors. This is the product.

nodes.label: Gate
nodes.note: Pass renders to the learner. Fail serves a validated item verbatim and queues the turn for human adjudication. The gate-fire rate is unknown and decides whether P2 is affordable.

nodes.label: Validated-item fallback
nodes.note: Examiner-written material served straight from the bank with no model in the path. It has to be a usable product, not a stub.

abs.why: The failure path needs no model, so the session degrades to validated material rather than stopping.

nodes.label: Turn logger
nodes.note: Citations, verdicts, gate result and twelve extracted style signatures, written at logging time rather than in a separate harness.

nodes.label: Rolling summariser
nodes.note: A bounded summary rather than full history, which is what keeps cost per turn near constant. It sits inside the content plane and its output is not citable evidence.

nodes.label: Adjudication queue
nodes.note: Every automated support failure is adjudicated by a person, which is what makes the groundedness number measurable rather than self-reported.

nodes.label: Escalation routing
nodes.note: Classifiers are bought; the policy and the routing are not. The policy is the part that cannot be outsourced.

nodes.label: Session caps
nodes.note: Listed in the safety plane beside classifiers and escalation routing, and set as a child-safety measure rather than as a cost control.

nodes.label: Billing and entitlement
nodes.note: Who has paid for what, and which learner profiles that entitles. Which entity holds the contract is unresolved.

nodes.label: Progress reporting
nodes.note: What the parent and the school are told, on what cadence, from the same mastery record the tutor itself uses.

nodes.label: Deterministic retrieval
nodes.note: The permitted set is fixed before generation and the model never searches. This is the single commitment everything else follows from.

nodes.label: Figure renderer
nodes.note: Diagrams rendered deterministically from a structured specification in the bank. A rendered figure inherits the item's validation and carries its source identifier by construction.

nodes.label: Computer algebra check
nodes.note: Every symbolically checkable step, checked locally with no model call. A disagreement is never overridden by the generator.

abs.why: Runs on no model at all, so no vendor or model behaviour change reaches it. D27.

nodes.label: Citation presence
nodes.note: A deterministic parse. Every sentence classified as a substantive curricular assertion must cite a node in the permitted set. Cheap to detect, and blocking.

nodes.label: Claim support
nodes.note: An entailment check on a pinned cheaper model, given the cited node and the assertion only.

nodes.label: Scope classifier
nodes.note: A classifier against the declared objective set. A question adjacent to the objective gets a refusal rather than an answer, which is the trade the whole product makes.

nodes.label: Style card renderer
nodes.note: Deterministic and versioned, mapping each dimension to a band and emitting the instruction for that band. The only path by which a card comes into existence.

nodes.label: Kill-switch read path
nodes.note: One boolean read per request, with a hard sixty-second cache ceiling. The flag is re-read at every turn, not at session start, which is why the bound is a turn and not a session.

abs.why: Every persona feature degrades to an archetype, so withdrawing a preset stops here. D11, proven by T-ZERO-01.

nodes.label: Signature extraction
nodes.note: Twelve counted signatures per turn. This is what turns a style claim into a measurement over live traffic rather than an assertion.

nodes.label: Mastery model
nodes.note: Unaided-check results on validated items, and the only input the grade range is allowed to read.

nodes.label: Paper assembler
nodes.note: Constraint satisfaction over the bank: mark total, coverage profile, command-word mix and difficulty distribution, excluding items seen recently.

nodes.label: Grade range mapper
nodes.note: An arithmetic mapping from performance to a band, with an evidence-sufficiency gate below which nothing is shown. Falsifiable, which a model estimate would not be.

nodes.label: Safety classification
nodes.note: Classifiers bought, policy and routing owned.

abs.why: The classifier is bought but the policy is not, so swapping a provider does not move the routing.

nodes.label: Item bank
nodes.note: Roughly 60 objectives and roughly 600 items at launch, as a planning figure rather than a count, every one examiner-validated before a learner sees it. The moat.

nodes.label: Objective graph
nodes.note: Specification reference, tier, prerequisites and must-warn misconceptions. A session teaches one of these, not a topic heading.

nodes.label: Validation records
nodes.note: Validator identity, date, result, notes and the date the item must be revalidated. The evidence behind P1.

nodes.label: Preset registry
nodes.note: One row per persona, and one boolean in that row is the entire kill switch.

nodes.label: Style objects
nodes.note: Twelve integers, a register note, a renderer version and a provenance record. It contains no creator material, which is the property that makes the rights position tractable.

nodes.label: Licence register
nodes.note: Term, schedules and status per preset. This is what the kill switch is enforcing.

nodes.label: Preset snapshot
nodes.note: The style object as it stood at session start, so a transcript can still be explained after a preset changes. Purged on the same seven-day line as the object itself.

nodes.label: Session and turn log
nodes.note: Citations, verdicts, gate result and style signatures per turn. Not browsable by anyone: access needs one of exactly three conditions and every access is logged with a reason.

nodes.label: Mastery state
nodes.note: Attempts, unaided passes, last seen, due. This is profiling, and there is no version of adaptive tutoring that avoids it.

nodes.label: Grade range record
nodes.note: Band, evidence count, coverage, and two booleans: sufficient, and calibrated, which is false at launch and stays false until a cohort sits a real examination.

nodes.label: Paper store
nodes.note: Assembled papers with their checks recorded, and the structural specification each was built to.

nodes.label: Learner profile
nodes.note: Year group, preset and per-subject adjustments. There is no date of birth field in this schema, anywhere, by design.

nodes.label: Account record
nodes.note: A verification boolean, a method identifier, a provider reference and a timestamp. No document, image or biometric is ever held.

nodes.label: Escalation records
nodes.note: Retention is longer than transcripts and is not yet set, because the safeguarding policy that would set it does not exist. A commitment with no number behind it.

nodes.label: DfE subject content
nodes.note: The published specification the bank is written from. The licence under which that may be done commercially is unanswered.

nodes.label: Board paper structure
nodes.note: Command words, mark tariffs, paper structure and time allowances, observed from papers we may not reproduce. The sharpest edge in the clean room.

nodes.label: Item writers
nodes.note: CINE writers working from the published subject content, never from board or textbook material. The writer and the validator are always different people.

nodes.label: Examiner validators
nodes.note: Current or recent examiners on terms that forbid bringing awarding-body material. A rate-limited human process that does not get cheaper when the next model ships.

nodes.label: Style raters
nodes.note: Three independent qualified raters per preset, scoring twelve dimensions without sight of each other, with a reliability gate and unfitted dimensions flagged rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Creator review right
nodes.note: The creator sees the twelve numbers and the rendered card and may object before the preset goes live. A term of the licence, not a courtesy.

nodes.label: Generator vendor
nodes.note: Pinned, abstracted, and disqualified regardless of model quality if zero-retention terms cannot be had.

nodes.label: Verifier vendor
nodes.note: Deliberately a different vendor from the generator. Two relationships to qualify instead of one, which is the price of not sharing a failure mode.

nodes.label: Age assurance provider
nodes.note: Certified to a recognised standard, returning a result rather than a document. We want a boolean, not an identity document sitting in our database.

nodes.label: Classifier vendor
nodes.note: Bought. The policy and the routing are not.

nodes.label: Payments
nodes.note: And the app stores, which are also the route by which a regulatory disruption order would arrive.

nodes.label: CDN and store metadata
nodes.note: Twenty-four hours in the kill-switch timetable, by a scripted purge rehearsed in advance rather than assembled on the day.

nodes.label: School identity provider
nodes.note: Route B. The school already knows who its pupils are, and age assurance largely dissolves as a problem.

nodes.label: Primer conversation
nodes.note: A why-question, spoken or typed, answered in one shape: a checked fact with its source, the harder bit, three positions at their strongest, the child's choice, their real question probed with evidence, and their own position read back. Each exchange closes with “Leave it there, or keep going?”, and keeping going stays within the time cap. Speech goes ahead of counsel's answer on OI-17 (D102).

nodes.label: Module switches
nodes.note: Parents switch the company's modules on and off; sensitive modules start off, while choices in a child's own future are on at every age from 8 unless a parent turns them off; nothing a parent writes reaches a child.

nodes.label: Idea and request channel
nodes.note: A parent may suggest a topic or a change. It goes to the company's review and is never shown to another user, which is what keeps the Online Safety Act position.

nodes.label: Parent activity record
nodes.note: Topics and modules used, each question as the catalogue question its entries answer, holding none of the child's words, and the child's position as the read-back. A declined question appears by its category and a stopped one only as “a personal question, stopped”; no full conversation is kept to show. A flagged exchange never reaches it (D26, T-PRM-08).

nodes.label: Explanation bank
nodes.note: Reviewed answers to children's why-questions by age band, each with its explainer's specification, and the evidence a choice needs: careers data, odds and the documented stories of named people, living ones by public facts from reviewed sources only. A figure no entry holds is never said; an estimate is said “roughly”; evidence follows the child's market; an unanswered question gets an honest not yet and becomes a request.

nodes.label: Inquiry packs
nodes.note: Three positions per question, each from a named thinker or tradition and each given its strongest case, never asserted as the Primer's own; the other two ask back as positions, never as people. Positions come from more than one culture across each module, not inside every question.

nodes.label: Module registry
nodes.note: The one list the composer reads, filtered by switch state and age band before anything is retrieved. Pulling a module is one operation. Each entry carries its market, so a child is offered only their own country's evidence, and the people it names, so that every entry naming one person can be pulled at once.

nodes.label: Record of ideas
nodes.note: The topic, each past question as the catalogue question its entries answer, holding none of the child's words, and the child's position as the read-back, which the child may correct before it is kept; carried from one session to the next. Nothing is kept word for word, no video is ever recorded, and nothing about family, the body or feelings is kept.

nodes.label: Attribution check
nodes.note: Every statement that a named thinker, tradition or other real person held a view or did something must be supported by a reviewed inquiry-pack or bank entry, quotations word for word. Blocking.

nodes.label: Contested-question check
nodes.note: On a question a pack marks contested, the Primer never states a conclusion as its own, however directly the child asks for one.

nodes.label: Personal-question triage
nodes.note: Sorts every turn, not only the first. A choice in the child's own future goes on under the fence; family, the body, feelings or safety stop, pointing the child to a trusted adult; a safeguarding signal is also flagged; when unsure, triage stops. A fuller review at the close reads the whole conversation, and flags the exchange when stops repeat across conversations.

nodes.label: Module writers and reviewers
nodes.note: Philosophy educators, teachers and subject specialists write; different people review, with a standing group for sensitive modules. Explainer specifications, and the careers data, odds and stories of living people a choice needs, add to what is written and reviewed. The Primer's rate limit.

nodes.label: Primer tablet
nodes.note: The Primer is its own tablet, one per child, locked to the Primer: no browser, no other apps, no notifications and no camera. Its microphone listens only while the child holds the talk key, and the screen shows plainly that it is listening; speech goes ahead of counsel's answer on OI-17 (D102).

nodes.label: Speech in and out
nodes.note: Turns a child's speech into text at once and throws the audio away, and speaks only text the checks have passed; a safety reply is shown, never spoken. Bought under zero retention; its recognition errors reach triage as the child's words. Goes ahead of counsel's answer on OI-17 under D102.

nodes.label: Drawn explainers
nodes.note: Draws each answer's explainer by code from its reviewed specification, building on screen in time with the voice, so a child sees the same drawing every time. Like the Tutor's figures, a drawing inherits its entry's review and source; no image or video model draws anything live.

nodes.label: Summaries, not records
nodes.note: At the close, keeps the read-back the child hears, in plain words and as the child corrects it, with the topic and the question as the catalogue question its entries answer, holding none of the child's words. Nothing the child says is kept word for word, except a flagged exchange, held for a trained reviewer and deleted when the review closes; no video is recorded.

nodes.label: Manner check
nodes.note: Runs on every turn, beside the attribution and contested-question checks, and blocks. “I”, “me”, “my”, “let's” and the child's display name are found by a deterministic match; praise, and a “we” that joins the Primer to the child, by a classifier, which is a weaker hold.

nodes.label: Explainer specifications
nodes.note: The reviewed specification behind each drawn explainer: what is drawn, in which steps, each keyed to a reviewed sentence of its entry or pack. Written and reviewed like the entries; an answer is served with its drawing or not at all.

nodes.label: Device duties
nodes.note: What a connected tablet for children must meet before sale in the UK and the US: product safety, connectable product security, radio rules and children's product certification. The register holds candidates only; the question is counsel's (OI-31).

nodes.label: Making the tablet
nodes.note: A stand-in tablet locked to the Primer for PM4; the dedicated tablet designed alongside and made only after PM4's evidence. Who designs and makes it is not decided.

nodes.label: No-direction check
nodes.note: In a conversation triage has sorted as a choice in the child's own future, blocks any sentence that tells the child what to do, predicts their own outcome, judges their chances from what they say about themselves, or encourages, discourages, warns or reassures them. A classifier, measured by T-PRM-06's blind raters: a gate, not a guarantee.

nodes.label: The own-future fence
nodes.note: The Primer may reason with a child about a choice in their own future, on by default from 8 to 13, neither encouraging nor discouraging: it sets out the reality from reviewed evidence and what the schools of thought say, then asks where the child stands. Family, the body, feelings and safety stay outside it and stop.

nodes.label: Personal questions, as met
nodes.note: A choice in the child's own future gets the reality and what the schools of thought say, and nothing more. A question about family, the body, feelings or safety stops with a pointer to a trusted adult, shown and never spoken, and only “Leave it there” follows.

nodes.label: Speech with a child
nodes.note: Children speak or type from launch, ahead of counsel's answer on OI-17 (D102), with speech off until the verified adult switches it on, and never before T-PRM-06's spoken battery has passed on recordings of children's speech. The Primer speaks in a stock synthetic voice cloned from no real person; a safety reply is shown, never spoken; the answer to a typed question is still spoken, so its subject reaches the room.

nodes.label: Primer screen
nodes.note: The screen as the films show it: the wake screen's one question and input box, the grey keyboard, each reply arriving whole on a card, with a small grey “Based on:” line under an answer's checked fact, and the two closing buttons of equal weight. A first-run screen at setup tells the child what the Primer is and what a parent can see.

nodes.label: An answer's shape
nodes.note: Every answer takes the whole shape, spoken and drawn at once: a checked fact with its source line, the harder bit, three positions at their strongest, the other two asking back as positions, the child's real question, probing with evidence, and the child's position read back.

nodes.label: Figures and named people
nodes.note: Every figure comes from a reviewed entry with its source, said “roughly” where the source estimates, and two figures that count different groups are never set in one comparison. A living person appears only by public, documented facts from reviewed sources, never their private life, and is never voiced.

nodes.label: Pulling from the Primer
nodes.note: A module, pack, entry, explainer or prompt pattern, or every entry that names one person, is pulled in one write to a live flag read at every turn; a conversation in flight falls back at its next turn.

nodes.label: The Primer's safeguarding review
nodes.note: A safety check on every turn and a fuller review at the close of each conversation (D107). A flagged exchange's words are held for a trained reviewer, who decides against a written policy whether and whom to inform, and are deleted when the review closes; the escalation record keeps none of the child's words.

nodes.label: The Primer's manner
nodes.note: The Primer never says “I”, never uses the child's name, never praises and never uses a “we” or “let's” that joins it to the child. It speaks as no one: its own voice is a stock synthetic voice, cloned from no one, and no character.

nodes.label: Measuring the Primer
nodes.note: How it would be known to work: every factual statement entailed by its entry, a child who disagrees not steered back, the manner check's account, and an independent evaluator's measure of how children reason, against a comparison group.

nodes.label: A Primer turn
nodes.note: From the talk key to the read-back: speech becomes text, triage sorts the turn, the composer selects the stage's entries, the generator places their reviewed sentences, every check blocks, and the gate renders the turn, spoken and drawn, or falls back. The close reads the child's position back; the logger keeps none of the child's words.

nodes.label: The Primer's named gaps
nodes.note: What the design does not yet close: a room hears an answer's subject; a reply shown on the screen can be read before the close; when stops repeat, the earlier stops' words are gone; nothing of a disclosure survives its review; a review that cannot run; the test recordings; US counsel and escalation.

nodes.label: Safeguarding count
nodes.note: For each child, the dates of earlier stops and flags and which each was, with no words and no subject, kept apart from the parent's record. Read only by the review at the close and the trained reviewer, never shown to the parent, and kept until the safeguarding policy's period ends, beyond a deletion request.

nodes.label: The Primer's escalation records
nodes.note: What a flagged exchange leaves once its review closes: the category the reviewer assigned, the dates, the reviewer's decision and whom they informed, and none of the child's words. Kept for a period that is unknown until the safeguarding policy sets it.

nodes.label: What a parent is promised
nodes.note: Fourteen promises to a parent in plain words, each beside the test that checks it, T-PRM-01 to T-PRM-14, all specified and none run.

nodes.label: One question, end to end
nodes.note: The worked example: a question about homework becomes a choice in the boy's own future, from a checked fact through three positions to his read-back and the close, annotated where it departs from the film.

nodes.label: Where the Primer's words come from
nodes.note: Every statement and drawing comes from a reviewed entry or pack; nothing is composed for speech alone; a child's words belong to the conversation, never to the content, and the read-back repeats a short phrase of theirs at most.

nodes.label: How the Primer differs
nodes.note: What sets the Primer apart from free AI tools: a tablet with nothing else on it, answers only from reviewed entries, no conclusion of its own, and a parent who sees the topics, each question as the catalogue question and the child's views as read-backs.

nodes.label: The Primer's milestones
nodes.note: PM1 to PM6, each complete when its evidence is in hand: the conditions for a child in any session, the test recordings licensed or made once counsel has answered on their lawful basis, and the stand-in tablet at PM4.

nodes.label: The Primer's risks
nodes.note: RP1 to RP9, each with its mitigation: a disclosure missed or reaching a parent, a child misheard, the tablet's cost, and reasoning about a child's own future reported as telling children what to do.

nodes.label: The Primer's cost per session
nodes.note: Speech in and out, triage, generation and up to seven checks per turn, the review at the close, and storage of the summaries, the log, the queues and the safeguarding stores; every figure Unknown until PM4.

nodes.label: Read-back check
nodes.note: Holds the read-back to what the child said: every statement of their view entailed by their words, none moved towards a position, no detail of family, friends, body or feelings, and no run of their words longer than a short phrase. Blocking.

nodes.label: Placed reviewed sentences
nodes.note: An explained stage holds only placed reviewed sentences, each compared with its entry word for word, so every one is drawn as its specification says; the generator's links and questions stand between explained stages. Blocking.

nodes.label: Not a companion
nodes.note: The Primer forms no relationship with a child: no “I”, no name, no praise, no reason to come back, and memory of ideas, never of a life; whether that keeps it outside the rules on companion chatbots is open.

nodes.label: What the Primer holds
nodes.note: The inventory of everything the Primer keeps, who sees it and for how long, with nothing kept that it does not list: summaries, settings, logs, queues, the flagged hold, the safeguarding count, escalation records and test recordings.

nodes.label: Desk unit
nodes.note: A camera on a flexible arm over each desk, set and locked at installation, angled at the page and the hand, never the face. No screen, speaker, light or microphone; nothing on the desk shows the child anything.

nodes.label: Teacher's class view
nodes.note: A desktop app on the teacher's Windows PC: one quiet tile per desk, amber when a child needs help, with plain words and a first triage. The teacher taps nothing during a lesson.

nodes.label: Error catalogue and task library
nodes.note: Reviewed entries for each kind of task: the known wrong procedures, written as computations, what each looks like in plain words, and a suggested next step.

nodes.label: Page and hand reader
nodes.note: Runs a face check first and discards any frame with a face; then reads characters as they are written and the grip from the hand. Recognises, never generates; keeps text, never the frame.

nodes.label: Class record and term summaries
nodes.note: What was read in each lesson, as text, and each child's term summary: the school's record, kept for the school year. No image, no notes typed about a child, no inferred condition, no ranking.

nodes.label: No voice kept; no camera at a face
nodes.note: The Primer hears a child only while the talk key is held and keeps no recording: speech becomes text at once and the audio is thrown away, going ahead of counsel's answer on OI-17 under D102. It has no camera. Foundation has no microphone; its camera sees the page and the hand, never the face, and keeps nothing it sees.

nodes.label: Self-tutor setup
nodes.note: Both consents first, from the verified adult and from the learner, then a live head-and-shoulders scan and a voice sample read from prompted sentences; no upload is accepted, and the feature stays off until both have consented.

nodes.label: Self-tutor
nodes.note: The tutor presented in the learner's own face and voice, in any archetype or an opted-in named preset, seen and heard by the learner alone, with the gated text always on screen.

nodes.label: Liveness check
nodes.note: Refuses replayed photographs, videos and recordings at capture, so a self-tutor can be made only of a person at the camera; its false-accept rate is unknown until M2.

nodes.label: Likeness store
nodes.note: The learner's face scan, voice sample and the render-time conditioning derived from them, held apart from every other store, encrypted, read only by the two renderers, and purged within seven days of a deletion.

nodes.label: Voice rendering
nodes.note: Speaks only text the gate has passed, one sentence at a time, in the learner's voice; conditioned at render time and never trained on the learner.

nodes.label: Face animation
nodes.note: Animates the head-and-shoulders likeness to the rendered speech; where it cannot meet the latency budget the learner sees a still likeness with speech instead.

nodes.label: Self-tutor deletion
nodes.note: One flag, set by the learner or the adult, read at every turn under the kill switch's sixty-second ceiling; rendering stops at the next turn and the likeness leaves primary stores within seven days.

nodes.label: Self-tutor stays private
nodes.note: No one but the learner may see or hear a self-tutor or obtain anything it renders; trigger T9 makes any path that would allow it a change-control gate.

nodes.label: Synthetic media labelling
nodes.note: Every clip the self-tutor renders carries a visible synthetic label and provenance metadata; which duties that meets in India, the UK and the US is open.

nodes.label: Speech and animation vendor
nodes.note: Bought, qualified at M2 and pinned like the model vendors, admitted only with render-time conditioning and zero retention, and excluded if it can reproduce a likeness only by fine-tuning.
